summary: Phakchok Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a Khenpo title at Dzongsar Institute and studied under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje. He serves as Vajra Master at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling.

Phanit Jetjiravat is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, where he was advised by Phra Suthithammanuwat, Veerachart Nimanong, and Paetpong Worapongpichet.

Philip A. Kuhn was a scholar of Sinology and history. Educated at Harvard, Georgetown, SOAS, and the Defense Language Institute, he served as associate professor at the University of Chicago (1963-1978) and center director at Harvard (1980-1986).

Philip A. Mellor works in religious and Buddhist studies. He completed a doctoral thesis at the University of Manchester by 1989 and served as Professor of Religion and Social Theory and Head of Humanities at the University of Leeds (attested 2010).

Philip Boas Yampolsky specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. After studying at Columbia University and under Yoshitaka Iriya, he served as a lecturer, adjunct associate professor, and librarian at Columbia (1968-1996).

Philip Clart is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied under Daniel L. Overmyer from approximately 1990 to 1996 and was appointed Professor of Chinese Culture and History at Leipzig University around 2008.
Philip Deslippe works in religious studies and Indology. Attested in 2020, he earned his PhD from the University of California, Santa Barbara, where he also held a position as a teaching associate.

Philip Kapleau was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki, Hakuun Ryōko Yasutani, Soen Nakagawa, and Sogaku Daiun Harada, and founded the Rochester Zen Center and Chapin Mill Retreat Center.

Philip L. Quinn was a philosophy and religious studies scholar. Educated at Georgetown, Delaware, and Pittsburgh, he served on the faculty at Brown University (~1976-1985) and held the John A. O'Brien Professorship at Notre Dame from 1985.

Philip Lutgendorf is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his B.A. from the University of Chicago (~1970-1987). He joined the University of Iowa in 1985 and served as president of the American Institute of Indian Studies (2010-2018).

Philip Whalen was active in Buddhist and religious studies. A Reed College graduate who studied under Richard Baker, he served as a visiting poet at Naropa University (~1974), head monk at Dharma Sangha (1984), and abbot at Hartford Street Zen Center (1991).

Philipp André Maas specializes in Indology and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Bonn in 2004 under Claus Vogel and Albrecht Wezler. He held posts at Bonn, the University of Vienna, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and Leipzig University.

Philippe Stern was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He held long-term posts at the Musée Guimet (1927-1965) and the École du Louvre (1929-1965), and was affiliated with the Musée de la parole et du geste around 1928.

Philippe Turenne is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at McGill University (attested 2010) under G. Victor Sōgen Hori, having also studied under Richard P. Hayes and several traditional teachers.

Philippe-Édouard Foucaux was a scholar in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held professorships in Tibetan at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (1842, 1854) and in Sanskrit at Collège de France (1857-1894).

Phillip E. Bloom works in Sinology, Japanology, and history and archaeology. Attested in 2013, he completed his PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Eugene Y. Wang, Yukio Lippit, and James Robson.

Phillip Zarrilli was a scholar in Indology and theatre. He served on the faculty at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from approximately 1979 to 2003 and subsequently held a post at the University of Exeter from approximately 2003 to 2020.

Phra Brahmapundit is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He was Rector of Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1997-2018), Chief Abbot at Wat Prayurawongsawat (~1996), and President of the International Council for the Day of Vesak (~2004).

Phra Medhidhammaporn is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Delhi by 1985 under the supervision of Margaret Chatterjee and Mahesh Tiwary.

Phra Rajavaramuni works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned degrees from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University and Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University, and served as Dean of Buddhist Studies and Deputy Vice Rector at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2012).
